Construct period life tables from age-specific mortality rates

Source: R/calculate_life_table.R
calculate_life_table.Rd

Constructs a period life table from input tables that provide age-specific mortality rates. Input data can come from user-provided input rate schedules, mortality process objects, or estimated rates from a simulation via calculate_mortality_rates(), and may be stratified by additional variables.

Usage

calculate_life_table(rates, radix = 1)

Arguments

rates

A table returned by calculate_mortality_rates(), a mortality process object from mortality(), or a data frame with at least age_start, age_end, and rate_mortality or rate columns. Must contain an open-ended age group specified by an Inf value for age_end. Input may be further stratified by other variables.

radix

Initial number of life-table survivors. Defaults to 1.

Value

A tibble containing standard life table parameters as well as sex and additional stratifying columns (when supplied).

Details

When the supplied rates table contains columns other than age_start, age_end, and either rate_mortality or rate, the function will treat these additional columns as stratifying dimensions and will stratify the output appropriately. It will also stratify output by time when time_start and time_end are included. The function also ignores additional calculated columns from the output of calculate_mortality_rates(), so the results of that function can be directly piped into this function. Stratification produces separate life tables by strata, not multistate life tables.

Constructed life tables do not make any adjustment to the \(a_x\) or \(q_x\) values for the 0 to 1 age group. commonly used in demographic methods. This is to ensure that results are consistent with input rates used by the simulation. Users who want to model changes in mortality within the first year of life can provide fractional year age bands for the first year of life.

Missing values on rates will result in missing values for lx, Lx, Tx, and ex for any later age bands. A zero mortality rate in the open age band will result in infinite life expectancy.

See also

calculate_life_expectancy() for life expectancy at selected ages.

Examples

data(usa_2000_mortality)

calculate_life_table(usa_2000_mortality)

#>    sex   age_start age_end       mx     n    ax       qx    lx lx_end       dx
#>    <chr>     <int>   <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl>

#>  6 f            20      25 0.000471     5 2.50  0.00235  0.989  0.987 0.00233

#> # ℹ 34 more rows
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: Lx <dbl>, Tx <dbl>, ex <dbl>

# stratify by groups to get stratified life tables
stratify_rates(
  usa_2000_mortality,
  by = list(ethnicity = c(A = 1.2, B = 0.9))
) |>
  calculate_life_table()
#> # A tibble: 88 × 14
